pressure.title: Water seals stop vapour and fire travelling
pressure.description: Open drains take non-pressurised spills, leaks and rainwater from paved, curbed areas. Each drain hub connects through a liquid seal (P-trap or sealed catch basin) so flammable vapour and flame cannot travel through the drain network from one area to another; seals must be kept topped up. Oily water flows to a sump and on to an oil–water separator; the skimmer removes floating oil.

video_tutorials.title: Open Drain System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Open Drain System.
An open drain system collects non-pressurised spills, leaks, wash water and rainwater from paved process areas through drain hubs and trenches.
Every inlet has a liquid seal so vapour and flame cannot travel through the network; oily water is collected in a sump, oil is skimmed and the water pumped to an oil-water separator.
Typical applications include process units, pump bays and loading areas; tank farms and utility areas with oil contamination.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Submersible Sump Pump with Float Switch → Oily-Water Separator.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Open Drain System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Open Drain System.
Top up seals; clear gratings.
Skim oil, desludge sump.
Inspect trench and seals.
Watch for dry seal: hydrocarbon smell in drains. Common cause: evaporation.
Watch for sump overflow: oil spread. Common cause: pump failure, heavy rain.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
